segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello and welcome to Real Easy English from BBC Learning English. I'm Neil.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And I'm Beth. In this podcast, we have a real conversation in easy English to help you learn.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: You can find the vocabulary from this episode and more to help you with your English at bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Hi Neil, how are things?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm very well, thank you Beth. How about you?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I'm very good, thank you. Now in today's episode, we are going to talk all about us.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, that's right. We'll help you learn to talk about yourself, your feelings and your personality.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK, so Neil, what do we mean by personality?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, we use the word personality to talk about the type of person we are.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So, how we behave, how we feel, how we think.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: For example, we can have a warm personality or a friendly personality.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK, so Neil, how would you describe yourself?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: what kind of personality do you have?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Ah that difficult Beth I think I quite calm laid back maybe I don get too upset or angry very easily

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: How about you, Beth? What's your personality?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I think that when I first meet people, I'm quite shy. I'm a bit quiet and I don't say much and maybe feel a bit nervous.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: But as soon as I get to know somebody, I am much more confident and then I'm very chatty and talkative.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So then I do talk a lot.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK, Beth. So can you tell me what your interests are, what you like doing?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well, I really like reading. I read quite a lot and I listen to audiobooks as well.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I find lots of different topics interesting

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And I also love going to the theatre

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I find that really exciting

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: What about you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I really like spending time with friends

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Chatting, having a laugh

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I really like live music too

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So Neil, you said you like going to watch live music

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Why do you enjoy that?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes I get really excited to see a new band that I like that I heard and I haven seen before And I think it also really exciting to hear live music because it exists just then that moment and it never repeated

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah, that's kind of why I love going to the theatre.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: It's special because it's just one performance.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Anything could happen and it's really exciting to just be there in the moment.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Now, when you're with your friends, I know that you laugh quite a lot. Would you say that you have a good sense of humour?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Maybe. Yes, I do. I like laughing and I think I like to see the funny side of things in the world.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So, usually everybody has a sense of humour. It just means the kind of things that you find funny.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah. And Beth, I remember once you told me you and your friend have a secret language.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We do. It's very silly. She made it up when she was a child and she taught me it. So sometimes we

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: have secret conversations and it's very silly and we find it very funny. I would say I have a silly

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: sense of humour.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well Beth I learned a lot about you today Shall we have a look at the vocabulary we used during our conversation

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yes So we had personality that is the type of person you are

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We've had sense of humour the types of things that make you laugh.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And throughout the conversation we have used adjectives that end in –ed and –ing.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: For example, Neil, you are excited to watch live music because you find the live music exciting.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We use adjectives that end with ED like excited and interested.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: When we mean our feelings, you are interested in something.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And we use adjectives that end in ING to talk about the thing that gives you that feeling.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: For example, you find live music exciting and I find reading books interesting.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: That's it for this episode of Real Easy English.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: If you want to learn more about how to talk about yourself,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: try one of our free Easy English courses.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: You can find them on our website bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Next time on Real Easy English, we'll talk about a very British topic, the weather.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: See you next time. Bye.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Bye.
